The direct callers of `ProgramWorkflowService.savePatientProgram` in the REST module are three resource classes, and one subclass inherits a caller. Nothing in the module's test sources calls the method directly. I didn't read the two test classes, so I can't say what they assert. The changed declaration I analysed is `ProgramWorkflowService.savePatientProgram` in openmrs-core, the interface method. Its implementation is `ProgramWorkflowServiceImpl.savePatientProgram`, which validates the patient, program and states before saving.

**Confirmed callers (best first)**

1. `openmrs-module-webservices.rest/omod/src/main/java/org/openmrs/module/webservices/rest/web/v1_0/resource/openmrs1_8/ProgramEnrollmentResource1_8.java` line 93. `save()` returns the result of `savePatientProgram(delegate)` directly, so any change to the return value or to validation changes the REST response for enrolment create and update. This is the main caller.
2. `openmrs-module-webservices.rest/omod/src/main/java/org/openmrs/module/webservices/rest/web/v1_0/resource/openmrs1_8/PatientStateResource1_8.java` line 115. `save()` adds the new state to the parent enrolment and then saves the parent. It depends on the save cascading the state and on the state validation in core.
3. `openmrs-module-webservices.rest/omod/src/main/java/org/openmrs/module/webservices/rest/web/v1_0/resource/openmrs1_8/PatientStateResource1_8.java` line 78. `delete()` voids the last state and saves the parent. It depends on the voided-state handling in core.
4. `openmrs-module-webservices.rest/omod/src/main/java/org/openmrs/module/webservices/rest/web/v1_0/resource/openmrs2_2/PatientProgramAttributeResource2_2.java` line 86. `save()` adds the attribute to the enrolment and saves the parent. It depends on the cascade of attributes.
5. `openmrs-module-webservices.rest/omod/src/main/java/org/openmrs/module/webservices/rest/web/v1_0/resource/openmrs2_2/PatientProgramAttributeResource2_2.java` line 65. `delete()` soft-deletes the attribute and saves the parent. It depends on how voided attributes are handled in core.

**Inherited caller**

6. `openmrs-module-webservices.rest/omod/src/main/java/org/openmrs/module/webservices/rest/web/v1_0/resource/openmrs1_10/ProgramEnrollmentResource1_10.java` line 40. This class extends `ProgramEnrollmentResource1_8`, so it inherits the `save()` at line 93 of the 1_8 class (item 1). I confirmed the inheritance from the class declaration; I did not read the file body.

**Core declarations involved**

- `openmrs-core/api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/api/ProgramWorkflowService.java` line 281. The interface method whose behaviour changed.
- `openmrs-core/api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/api/impl/ProgramWorkflowServiceImpl.java` line 248. The implementation. Its validation at lines 250–264 is the code path that a behaviour change would most likely touch.

**Likely but unverified**

- The REST framework dispatches POST, PUT and DELETE to these resources' `save()` and `delete()` methods. I did not read the framework's dispatch code, so the request-level effect is inferred.
- `ProgramEnrollmentResource2_2` is the parent of `PatientProgramAttributeResource2_2`. Its file did not show up in the search, so I haven't checked whether it calls the service method.
- The test classes `PatientStateResource1_8Test` and `PatientProgramAttributeResource2_2Test` exercise items 2–5 indirectly. I did not open them.

**Not checked**

- openmrs-core's own callers, such as the `ProgramWorkflowDAO` and `HibernateProgramWorkflowDAO` definitions and any core services that call the method. Those are outside this question's scope.
- The other REST-facing repositories (for example openmrs-esm-patient-chart, which calls the REST API over HTTP). A change in the Java return value or validation would reach them only through the JSON contract, and I haven't searched their field names.
- Reflection or dynamic dispatch through the `@Resource` and `@SubResource` annotations. I did not check that the annotations make the framework call anything other than the overridden methods above.
